entries.title: As freed ComEd defendants face new trial, jurors say they already considered ‘every aspect’ of the case
entries.summary: <p>Before they <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/comed-bribery-trial/2026/04/14/madigan-bribery-comed-conspiracy-bribery-chicago-crime-pramaggiore-mcclain" target="_blank" >freed two former ComEd officials</a> who went to prison over an alleged corruption scheme<b> </b>involving Illinois’ most powerful politician, federal appeals court judges asked a lot of questions about the case — but mostly <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2023/11/3/23919713/corruption-jurors-ed-burke-trial" target="_blank" >about the jury</a> that found the pair guilty.</p><p>For example, how could the judges be sure the jury didn’t focus solely on bribery claims that have since been undermined by the U.S. Supreme Court?</p><p>The Chicago Sun-Times asked three of the 12 jurors Wednesday. They said they carefully considered every claim leveled against former ComEd CEO Anne<b> </b>Pramaggiore and longtime ComEd lobbyist Michael McClain — including those that survived a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-corruption-trials/2024/06/26/supreme-court-snyder-ruling-madigan-corruption" target="_blank" >2024 Supreme Court ruling</a>.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/comed-bribery-trial/2026/04/14/madigan-bribery-comed-conspiracy-bribery-chicago-crime-pramaggiore-mcclain" >Ex-ComEd CEO, Madigan ally to be freed from prison as appeals court calls for new trial in conspiracy case</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>“We concluded they all intertwined and related to each other,” Robert<b> </b>Garnes, one of the jurors in the 2023 ComEd conspiracy trial, told the Sun-Times.</p><p>The ComEd trial <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2023/5/2/23697452/jurors-reach-verdict-in-comed-bribery-trial" target="_blank" >ended with the convictions</a> of McClain, Pramaggiore<b> </b>and two others of a plot to bribe<b> </b>ex-Illinois House Speaker <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/madigan-trial-news" target="_blank" >Michael J. Madigan</a>. The high court’s later decision to limit a key bribery law undermined the verdict and led to the dismissal of the bribery counts in 2025. But convictions for conspiracy and falsifying books and records remained.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-floatRight> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a entries.title: Sky's Skylar Diggins wanted to be closer to home, but she’s not just coasting into retirement
entries.summary: <p>To be a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> fan right now is to be bursting with questions. Ones like: What is Skylar Diggins doing in Chicago?</p><p>It surprised many to see the seven-time All-Star choose a team that has won less than 30% of its games over the last two seasons, and an organization not exactly known for flawless execution since its 2021 championship.</p><p>So how did she end up here?</p><p>As the new collective-bargaining agreement reshaped the league this offseason, Diggins took a moment to reflect.</p><p>She thought about where she was in her career — 35 years old, two kids, entering her 12th season — and decided she wanted a change. She's played on the West Coast her whole career, but she grew up in South Bend, 90 miles outside of Chicago.</p><p>She wanted to be closer to home.</p><p>And Chicago successfully sold her on its vision: a win-now roster that was tougher, more athletic, more competitive than last year.</p><p>For head coach Tyler Marsh, Diggins' arrival is proof the organization is moving in the right direction.</p><p>"Skylar has been around this league a long time to know the fake from the real," Marsh said. "And there's a reason she wanted to be here. Being close to home helps, but you also gotta be able to trust the people you're going to compete with. There's some discernment there that she's able to recognize."</p><p>The Sky did execute well in free agency, landing <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky/2026/04/14/azura-stevens-returns-to-chicago-where-the-fit-and-the-money-made-sense" >stretch big Azurá Stevens</a> and two-way wing DiJonai Carrington, and adding young talent in Rickea Jackson and Jacy Sheldon.</p><p>But executing the "win-now" part won't be easy. Most of the league's top teams retained their cores. And even with all the added talent, Diggins is still the Sky's only All-Star.</p><p>Which means the Sky better hope she didn't come back to the Midwest just to decompress before retiring.</p><p>Lucky for them, she shot down the idea before anyone thought to raise it.</p><p>"I'm not just coming here saying this is the end or whatever for me," she said at her introductory news conference. "I don't think it'll be a diminishing return. I'm committed to the work. … I want to get better. That's been my mantra since I was a kid — 'get better.' That's the mindset I have here for this organization, for myself, and that's the standard I hold myself to."</p><p>Even for players with the highest standards, some decline in their game is inevitable. Over the last two years, Diggins' scoring average has settled around 15, down from the 17-20 range of her prime. But pair that with six assists and you're still looking at one of the best point guards in the league.</p><p>So, Sky fans: is this great-player-comes-home-at-the-tail-end-of-her-career storyline giving anyone a Candace Parker flashback? Will this homecoming end in a championship, too?</p><p>One can hope. But there are a few big differences between then and now. As good as Diggins is, she's not quite Parker. And Parker came home to a roster that had been together for years. Diggins is walking into a complete overhaul.</p><p>She'll need a little magic to bring them together ahead of schedule.</p><p></p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module entries.title: After quick struggles for Shane Smith, White Sox aim to 'slow down his world' at Triple-A
entries.summary: <p>After an awful opening week, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>White Sox</u></a>’ starting rotation has been a bright spot with an MLB-best 1.73 ERA in 11 games from April 3-14.</p><p>If you were told in spring training that Sox starters would go on a heater like that, you probably would’ve expected Opening Day hurler <b>Shane Smith </b>to be on top of his game — not down on the farm trying to rediscover his All-Star form from last season.</p><p>For Smith to run it back to the big leagues, he’s got to stop running away from the pitch that made him a Rule 5 success story, general manager <b>Chris Getz</b> said a week after the surprising demotion.</p><p>“He was running away from using his four-seam fastball. Just the overall quality of that pitch, along with his curveball, just wasn't up to his standard,” Getz said of the righty, who covered only 8⅓ innings in his three Sox starts, surrendering 12 runs before <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports/2026/04/08/white-sox-option-opening-day-starter-shane-smith-to-triple-a-charlotte" target="_blank" ><u>getting shipped to Triple-A Charlotte</u></a>. “We felt like it was best to kind of slow down his world a little bit, get him in an environment that is not so focused on getting so deep into games, or even win the ballgame."</p><p>Smith looked a little better in his last big-league game, but had another uneven outing in his first go with the Knights over the weekend, giving up three runs on four hits with a walk and five strikeouts in four innings.</p><p>“There’s always a cascade effect when you have starters not going deep into games. It starts affecting bullpens,” Getz said. “He definitely made progress in the most recent outing up here at the major league level, but we know that he can be so much better, and he acknowledges that as well.”</p><h3><b>Pre-game scare</b></h3><p>Attendees at Rate Field were left in a stunned silence before Wednesday’s game when <b>Gerald Chaney</b> collapsed while singing "Lift Every Voice and Sing” on Jackie Robinson Day.</p><p>Chaney, a longtime national anthem performer and beloved ballpark presence, was alert as paramedics treated him on the field. He was taken to a hospital for further evaluation and treatment, according to the Sox.</p><h3><b>Schultz in the rotation</b></h3><p>Manager <b>Will Venable</b> confirmed that rookie lefty <b>Noah Schultz</b> has a regular spot in the Sox’ starting rotation after his <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/14/noah-schultz-white-sox-mlb-debut" target="_blank" ><u>shaky MLB debut</u></a> Tuesday night — no surprise, but an assertion that Getz stopped short of making a day earlier.</p><p>Schultz consistently flashed 98 on the radar gun and struck out four while laboring through 4⅓ innings, giving up four runs but rebounding from some first-inning jitters.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure ><u>growing up in Aurora</u></a>.</p><p>“They helped get that competitive spirit in me. It started at a young age,” Schultz said. “I can’t thank them enough. They have been with me through it all. It’s so awesome to have their support and have them in the stands.”</p><h3><b>Coming and going</b></h3><p>As part of the Sox’ <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/15/sam-antonacci-called-up-white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>latest roster shuffle</u></a> bringing up prospect <b>Sam Antonacci</b>, they also recalled veteran lefty reliever <b>Tyler Gilbert</b>, optioned <b>Brandon Eisert</b> to Charlotte and designated outfielder <b>Dustin Harris</b> for assignment.</p><p>Harris was a hero of Sunday’s win at Kansas City, robbing a potential home run in right field. He went 3-for-12 with a double, four walks and a pair of stolen bases in six games with the Sox.</p><p>Venable said they’ll send him to Charlotte if he clears waivers.</p><p>“It was a really tough entries.title: White Sox national anthem performer Gerald Chaney back to singing after pre-game collapse
entries.summary: <p>Attendees at Rate Field were left in a stunned silence before Wednesday’s White Sox game when Gerald Chaney collapsed while singing “Lift Every Voice and Sing” on Jackie Robinson Day.</p><p>Chaney, a longtime national anthem performer and beloved ballpark presence, was alert as paramedics treated him on the field. He was taken to a hospital for evaluation and doing well by the end of the game — “even singing,” according to the Sox.</p><p>“The entire White Sox family is sending love to Gerald and his family for a full and speedy recovery,” the team said in a statement.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-600000" name="image-600000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/e88797b/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1800x1010+0+0/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F10%2Fa7%2F3c33490947b3a7b987657b17d485%2Fsox-cst-062412-4.JPG 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/51cfee9/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1800x1010+0+0/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F10%2Fa7%2F3c33490947b3a7b987657b17d485%2Fsox-cst-062412-4.JPG 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/fc0eb07/2147483647/strip/true/crop/1800x1010+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2F10%2Fa7%2F3c33490947b3a7b987657b17d485%2Fsox-cst-062412-4.JPG" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="Gerald Chaney, pictured singing the national anthem before a Sox game on June 22, 2012. entries.title: White Sox call up Sam Antonacci looking for jolt to stagnant offense
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" ><u>White Sox</u></a> prospect Sam Antonacci got news of his promotion from Triple-A Charlotte about 20 hours before he took the field for his debut at Rate Field on Wednesday. </p><p>“Tired, but adrenaline high,” the Springfield native said inside his first big-league clubhouse after a whirlwind travel day. “Get a cup of coffee in you and you’re good to go.”</p><p>It worked for him while playing <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/03/19/sam-antonacci-returns-to-spring-training-says-wbc-experience-was-definitely-worth-it" >for Team Italy</a>, whose run to the World Baseball Classic semifinal was famously fueled by a dugout espresso machine also enjoyed by another caffeine-cranked Sox player, Kyle Teel.</p><p>Now the Sox are looking for a shot in the arm offensively from Antonacci, a utility player whose hot bat to start the year made him the club’s second key prospect call-up in as many days, following the debut of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/04/14/noah-schultz-white-sox-mlb-debut" target="_blank" ><u>prized left-hander Noah Schultz</u></a>.</p><p>“Excited to add his energy and his skillset to the group,” manager Will Venable said. “He's gonna play extremely hard, control the zone, play solid defense and run the bases extremely well.”</p><p>The Sox’ No. 9-rated prospect wasted little time checking some of those boxes with his parents, sister and 10,192 of his newest fans in attendance. Antonacci vacuumed up a grounder to second base for his first big-league defensive assist to close the first inning, and then dropped a single into right field in his first career at-bat to open the Sox’ half of the second on Wednesday against the Rays. </p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">First big league hit for Sam Antonacci! <a href="https://t.co/p2h7zrD4DF">pic.twitter.com/p2h7zrD4DF</a></p>— Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) <a href="https://twitter.com/whitesox/status/2044572659208400997?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">April 16, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.twitter.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Later in his 1-for-3 night, he made a diving stop on a hot grounder up the middle, and drew a ninth-inning walk that started the Sox' only offensive onslaught during an otherwise lifeless 8-3 loss that saw catcher Reese McGuire pitching in garbage time.</p><p>"It was a dream come true, to be honest. Obviously not the end result," Antonacci said. "As much as I like to be even-keeled and keep my head on straight with the job at task, I needed to take a step back and really take it all in, because I’m living out a dream I had when I was a little kid."</p><p>Though the 2024 fifth-round draft pick debuted at second, he got to the Sox three weeks into the season because he was learning left field on the job at Charlotte, fast-tracking his path in an organization lacking outfield depth. Antonacci mostly played second last year across three levels of the farm system. </p><p>Venable said he had him batting fifth and playing second in his debut only because it coincided with a previously scheduled day off for regular Chase Meidroth.</p><p>"It's really quality at-bats, where he's making good swing decisions, really grinding," Venable said of his newest rookie.</p><p>While Schultz joins a starting rotation that has been surprisingly sturdy, a stagnant Sox offense is desperate for a spark from Antonacci. He joined a team sitting dead last in baseball in batting average (.192), on-base percentage (.281), slugging percentage (.305), hits (107) and runs (54).</p><p>Antonacci’s call-up was hastened by his .313/.500/.479 (15-for-48) start with the Knights, with two doubles, two home runs, seven RBI and five stolen bases.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" entries.title: 2 teen girls arrested, accused of battering Cook County sheriff's deputies
entries.summary: <p>Two 15-year-old girls were arrested after allegedly battering Cook County sheriff's officers responding to reports of gunfire in Woodlawn Wednesday afternoon, according to Chicago police.</p><p>The sheriff's officers were in the 6400 block of South Evans Avenue at 4:41 p.m. when they saw several people fighting. When they tried to intervene, the two teens allegedly battered the officers, police said. The teens were arrested at the scene.</p><p>One officer was taken to St. Bernard Hospital in good condition, police said.</p>

entries.title: Nico Hoerner, Matt Shaw dominate as Cubs grab series win over Phillies
entries.summary: <p>PHILADELPHIA —<b> Matt Shaw</b> and <b>Nico Hoerner</b> formed quite the duo in the Cubs' Wednesday’s 11-2 win.</p><p>Shaw would double, and Hoerner drove him in.</p><p>Hoerner's table-setting ways have been pronounced in the last two games of the Phillies series. His eight RBIs over the past two games were the most he’s recorded over a two-game span. The offense is at its best when it strings together hits and has productive at-bats, particularly from the bottom of the order. On all three of Shaw’s doubles, Hoerner drove him in.</p><p>“I thought it was a big night for Matt,” manager Craig Counsell said. “When your No. 9 hitter gets three doubles, that's a good sign.”</p><p>Hoerner was 3-for-5 with a career-high five RBIs. Shaw was 3-for-4 with two RBIs. The ideal version of the Cubs’ lineup involves production from the entire lineup. With first-round picks at six spots, the group has the pedigree and talent to be a problem on a daily basis.</p><p>If the hitters start producing towards their career norms then the offense should be able to carry the bulk of the responsibility while the pitching staff is depleted.</p><p>“We should go out there and expect to have good at-bats,” Shaw said. Things are starting to fall a little bit, so t's awesome to get some momentum and have the boys run.”</p><p><b>Imanaga dealing</b></p><p>As of late, left-hander<b> Shota Imanaga </b>has resembled the pitcher who took MLB by storm in 2024.</p><p>Wednesday’s start got off to an inauspicious start. Imanaga allowed a leadoff homer to Trea Turner, but that was the extent of the damage he allowed Wednesday. Imanaga regrouped and mowed through the Phillies’ lineup. He allowed one run on three hits with one walk and 11 strikeouts. His four-seamer sat at 92 mph.</p><p>“We talk so much about velocity in general,” Hoerner said, “I think it is different with him throwing 93 instead of 90. Every bit of life on that four-seamer he has is a huge deal.”</p><p>Imanaga is pitching with the confidence he seemingly lost toward the end of last season. His 26 whiffs were tied for the most in one outing by a Cubs pitcher in the pitch-tracking era — <b>Yu Darvish</b> also recorded 26 against the White Sox in 2020.</p><p><b>Injury report</b></p><p>The Cubs’ injury report seemingly grows longer by the day. Cubs manager <b>Craig Counsell </b>announced that right-hander <b>Porter Hodge</b> would miss the rest of the season after having UCL reconstruction surgery.</p><p>• Opening Day starter <b>Matthew Boyd</b> is headed to Ohio and will pitch on Thursday for Triple-A Iowa. That puts him on schedule to return to the Cubs around next Wednesday to finish a seven-game homestand against the Phillies.</p><p>• Left-hander <b>Jordan Wicks</b> (left elbow inflammation) is scheduled to pitch Saturday for Triple-A Iowa. He’s been out since spring training.</p><p>• Right-hander<b> Hunter Harvey </b>(right triceps inflammation)<b> </b>is likely going to take longer than the 15 days on the IL. Counsell that Harvey is in strengthening mode.</p><p>• Right-hander <b>Phil Maton</b> (right knee tendinitis) had an optimistic update. Counsell said he’s recovering each day. Phil didn’t stop throwing after he was placed on the 15-day IL, so now it’s a matter of getting the arm back to game action.<br></p>

entries.title: Jed Hoyer to 'come up with real options' for Cubs' injured pitching staff
entries.summary: <p>PHILADELPHIA — Injuries have put <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> president of baseball operations Jed Hoyer on the prowl for starting pitching.</p><p>“You just immediately feel sorry for the player, but then you just process like, ‘Who’s up next?’ ” Hoyer said before the game Wednesday against the Phillies. “You have to move on quick mentally. It sounds cold-hearted, but that’s the nature of the job. The games go on, you have to find replacements.”</p><p>Cubs manager Craig Counsell announced that right-handed reliever Porter Hodge suffered a setback recovering from a flexor strain and will miss the rest of the season after undergoing surgery on his ulnar collateral ligament. He began the season on the 15-day injured list and was seen as a player who could help the team.</p><p>Hodge, whom the Cubs thought could rebound from a rough 2025 season (6.27 ERA), now joins promising right-hander Cade Horton as pitchers lost for the season. Hoyer said that Hodge felt some discomfort early in spring training.</p><p>With relievers Ethan Roberts (middle finger laceration), Hunter Harvey (right triceps) and Phil Maton (knee) all sidelined, the Cubs’ bullpen has become increasingly unbalanced with an unusually large number of left-handers. Given the sheer number of injuries, it’s fair to wonder if the Cubs are assessing their own pitching processes.</p><p>“You have to take a look because you wouldn’t be doing your job if you didn’t,” Hoyer said. “A lot of guys go down these days. Guys throw so unbelievably hard, but we’ll do a deep dive and see if there’s a commonality to the injuries.”</p><p>Entering Wednesday, Cubs relievers had the 15th-best ERA in baseball (4.04). Left-hander Riley Martin has helped the Cubs survive this stretch (4„ scoreless innings).</p><p>Hoyer said that the club is looking at the injuries as an opportunity for others to emerge. Hodge wasn’t on the Cubs’ radar early in the 2024 season, but he received a chance to show how he could deliver in the majors and ran with it (1.88 ERA).</p><p>“There’s opportunities being created for guys,” Counsell said. “Through this process, we’re going to find some guys that are going to help us this year, and so that’s how you’ve got to look at it. That’s a great thing. That’s a positive out of all this.”</p><p>The offense’s improvement also should help the pitching staff. The way hitters were aggressive and opportunistic in Tuesday’s 10-4 win over the Phillies is how many envisioned the offense before the season. Right-hander Colin Rea, who pitched six innings and allowed three runs, said the offensive production made it easier for him to pitch.</p> <p>“Somehow, our run-scoring numbers aren’t that bad,” Hoyer said. “But I think [when] we look up and down the lineup, you have so many guys that are so far below career norms, especially in [slugging] — I look at it as a real opportunity. I’m almost excited about it because we’re 17 games in [and] only a couple guys are sort of above their projections.”</p><p>As the offense finds its footing, Hoyer has to survey the market for capable replacements.</p><p>“The schedule’s not gonna stop,” Hoyer said. “We gotta find ways to come up with new guys and come up with real options. entries.title: Blackhawks owner Danny Wirtz announces contract extension for GM Kyle Davidson
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" >Blackhawks</a> owner Danny Wirtz announced a multi-year contract extension Wednesday for general manager Kyle Davidson, who's wrapping up his fourth season in the position.</p><p>GM contracts are generally extended consistently until they're fired — it's rare to see one leave an NHL team simply because his contract expired — but it's still notable.</p><p>Wirtz also gave Davidson a firm and extensive vote of confidence on the Chicago Sports Network pregame show.</p><p>"Kyle has done everything we've expected of him," Wirtz said. "When he got the job, his first task was to rebuild our prospect pool. ... He very systematically, very confidently built that to where I believe, right now, we have the best prospect pool in the NHL. Many of those prospects are now actually NHL players, contributing and highly impactful on our team."</p><p>"But at the same time, we didn't hire Kyle to be the prospect GM. He's building a championship-caliber team. It goes to the point we've extended Kyle's contract. We are committing to Kyle to continue the plan he's put in place. We feel confident in that. We believe has the right insight, right team around him and the belief he can continue to build a championship team."</p><p>In a news conference later, Wirtz mentioned the Hawks being more competitive on the ice this season, improving their point total despite losing a plethora of close games, as a sign of improvement.</p><p>Of course, that competitiveness hasn't held true over the past month, during which time the roster has most closely resembled the long-term roster. But Wirtz said he wasn't alarmed by that.</p><p>"[It's] probably a reminder and a recognition of just how hard this league is, especially for players going from leagues where they play considerably less games, less travel," he said.</p><p>"I don’t think that, in any way, shakes my confidence for the team that’s being built... I expect them to continue to grow next season."</p><p>He conceded he would be disappointed next season if the Hawks "stayed flat to this year" and finished in the league's bottom-five again.</p><p>And he clarified Davidson has a green light to make significant trades this summer if the opportunity arises: "There’s nothing holding Kyle back, that’s for sure. It’s not coming from me."</p><p>But he continues to focus most of his attention well into the future.</p><p>"These players, in their own development, have to take another step," Wirtz said. "Even Connor [Bedard] needs to take another step, and he will. He’s that competitive. </p><p>"The collective improvement each of those players makes translates into team competitiveness and ultimately wins. That’s what we’re going for. Our intention is to be competing for and winning Stanley Cups, but we can’t race to that conclusion until we do all those right things."</p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module entries.title: 2 teens shot, 1 fatally, at Woodlawn bus stop
entries.summary: <p>Two teens were shot, one fatally, at a bus stop in Woodlawn Wednesday afternoon, according to Chicago police.</p><p>The teens, a boy and girl, both 16, were at a bus stop in the 6300 block of South Stony Island Avenue at 3:23 p.m. when a person approached and opened fire, police said. The boy was hit multiple times and taken to University of Chicago Medical Center in critical condition; he later died.</p><p>The girl was shot in her left leg and also taken to University of Chicago Medical Center in fair condition, police said. No one is in custody.</p><p></p><p>Chicago Police Supt. Larry Snelling addressed recent incidents of violence involving young people during a hearing on the federal consent decree Tuesday.</p><p>“We have young kids who are now taking to the streets, not only in Chicago but across the country ... and they’re engaging in activity that has led to violence,” Snelling said.</p><p>Snelling said the police department had seen "more CPS students shot and killed this year than we have in the past 10 years, possibly." According to Chicago Police Department homicide data, 2026 is on track to see the third consecutive year in which youth homicides have fallen by mid-April with 13.</p><p>The city saw 13 youth homicides by this point in the year in 2019 and 2020, though that number nearly doubled in 2023, reaching 24. The tally for the same time period dropped in 2024 and has continued to decline since. entries.title: Blackhawks end season with feel-good comeback win over Sharks
entries.summary: <p>The first two periods of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a>' season finale Wednesday mirrored their last few weeks: Sloppy, slow and worrying.</p><p>Then a lucky goal off Sam Rinzel's stick late in the second period shifted momentum, and it seemed the Hawks suddenly discovered an extra reserve energy tank, racing away for a 5-2 win over the Sharks.</p><p>They dominated the third period, getting two beautiful goals from Louis Crevier, two assists from Connor Bedard (both saucy backhand passes) and a redemption goal by Ryan Greene, who had missed an empty net earlier.</p><p>"We wanted to finish on a good note, even though the last couple weeks have been hard," Crevier said. "It doesn't erase what happened, but we showed some character in the third."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Bedard sets up Crevier for the game-tying goal 😮‍💨 <a href="https://t.co/qgpUIGRr6H">pic.twitter.com/qgpUIGRr6H</a></p>— Blackhawks on CHSN (@CHSN_Blackhawks) <a href="https://twitter.com/CHSN_Blackhawks/status/2044606274117988549?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">April 16, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.twitter.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Wednesday's result marked the first time the Sharks, demoralized after getting eliminated from playoff contention Monday, lost in regulation after leading at the second intermission all season. </p><p>It also marked just the Hawks' fourth win in their last 18 home games. They finished the season 29-39-14, earning 72 points — up from 61 last season.</p><p>"We were never checked out or anything like that," Bedard said. "We were trying every game. That’s something we want people to know. Obviously [it] didn’t go our way, but there wasn’t a day where we weren’t trying to do everything we can to put out our best effort.</p><p>"Coming into this last game, we really wanted to...show our fans just how much pride we have in playing in the NHL but also playing in Chicago. I’m happy we were able to do that and have a win to end the year."</p><p>Crevier delivered a heroic performance, not only with the two goals but also two crucial blocks on a third-period penalty kill, as he bounced back from what he called one of his worst performances of the season <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/04/13/blackhawks-sabres-effort-levels-crash-frank-nazar-ryan-greene" target="_blank" >Monday</a> against the Sabres.</p><p>His evolution from seventh defenseman into top-four regular was one of the more satisfying under-the-radar trends of this Hawks season. As coach Jeff Blashill put it, "Mental toughness is a huge part of individual success."</p>
